column1: # Tunisia, the Institut National de la Météorologie (meteo.tn), per delegation at INM's own
# reference points, the units' points (profiles-tested.md, data-maghreb-libya). Africa/Tunis.
# Standard Asr. Sunrise comes from INM's ephemeris endpoint every third day ('-' on the others). The
# Fajr printed is when the fast begins (F+E); these tables print no imsak, and the app shows none for Tunisia
# (ruling R188, the owner, 12 Nov 2026: no promise of an imsak INM does not print; the end of eating stands alone).
# Split: fit on the four low delegations' 2026 (Tunis and Sfax every day, Tabarka and Ben Guerdane
# every third day); held out, Tunis 2019–2026 (eight days a year, at INM's earlier point for Tunis)
# and the elevated delegations Tataouine and Tala. Their dips (0.45°, 1.0°) and the dipped Fajr's
# 60 s were found on these same tables in the research, so those rows check the national margins
# with the dips, not the dips themselves.
# Not rows: tn_tunis_2026.txt, agentB/tunis_inm.txt, off-tunis.txt, tn_tunis1.txt and tn_tala.txt
# repeat the same days.
# The weekly monitor's running captures (archive/tables/monitor/tn-inm/<delegation>.txt, begun 28 Sep 2026: each
# fetch adds the coming seven days with INM's sunrise on each, and the gate reads the file as it stands), held out
# where they add days: Tabarka, Ben Guerdane and Tala, whose yearly tables print every third day. Tunis's, Sfax's
# and Tataouine's captures repeat their yearly rows' days through 2026 (the same minutes; they add only INM's
# sunrise on the days between), so they are not rows yet: prove adds each as a row by itself (recipes.tsv, tn-inm)
# on the first run whose capture prints a day the yearly row does not hold, which is January 2027.
